AWPTCM-T33243.objective:
• A gratuitous ARP is transmitted after an interface link transitions to Up (default delay 5 seconds).
  • The gratuitous ARP transmission delay is configurable via the gratuitous-arp-link timer.
  • Setting gratuitous-arp-link to 0 disables gratuitous ARP transmission on link up.
  • Gratuitous ARP is sent on link up for IP interfaces, tagged ports, and static/dynamic channels.
  • Gratuitous ARP is sent after system startup and after hot-swap insertion of modules/ports.
  • ARP and neighbour tables are updated correctly after a gratuitous ARP is sent.
  • Static ARP entries remain intact and functional after a gratuitous ARP event on the same interface.

steps.description: The testing for this is covered by the auto test : https://wiki.atlnz.lc/awpwiki/index.php/1351. Note: the automated test covers multiple test cases. Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
Configure an IP interface and bring the link up (or perform shutdown/no shutdown). Confirm a gratuitous ARP is transmitted after the configured gratuitous-arp-link delay (default 5 seconds).
Set a non-default gratuitous-arp-link timer value. Bring the link up and confirm the gratuitous ARP is sent at the configured interval.
Set gratuitous-arp-link to 0. Bring the link up and confirm no gratuitous ARP is transmitted.
Test gratuitous ARP on tagged ports and on static/dynamic channel-groups. Confirm transmission occurs when the whole logical interface transitions.
Perform multiple link up/down cycles, startup, and hot-swap where supported. Confirm gratuitous ARP is sent for each affected IP interface.
Verify ARP and neighbour tables are updated correctly after gratuitous ARP transmission, and that any static ARP entries remain intact.
